utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, ladies and gentlemen; good morning to the technical booth, the interpreters, legal assistants, registrar; good morning, counsel for the Prosecution, counsel for Defence; good morning to you, General Krstic. We are five minutes late to begin our hearing today, but we will try and stick to the new timetable today and in the following days as well, of course, bearing in mind the health condition of General Krstic. We will be working in blocks of one hour and a half with half-hour breaks, and the last break will last one hour. The most important reason for this break was, actually this long break, the one-hour break, so that we can all work and have lunch. So I should like to suggest the following: Instead of having one hour and a half blocks of work, that we should proceed with 45 minutes of work, which will enable General Krstic to have more short breaks, and instead of having one-half-hour break, we will have two 15-minute breaks. So we will use the same timetable but with a different length of breaks; that is to say, we will be working until quarter past ten. Afterwards, we will have a 15-minute break, and we will resume at 10.30. We will work until 11.15, which will be followed by another 15-minute break, and the next block of work will start at half past eleven, and we will work until quarter past twelve. After that block, we will have another 15-minute break. We will resume at half past twelve and work until quarter past one. After that, we will have a long break, one-hour break, and we will resume at quarter past two and work until 3.00. So actually, we will have three 15-minute breaks. When I said at the beginning that we were five minutes late, I was perfectly aware that if we have several breaks, we also run the risk of starting late. So I appeal to all of you to start -- to be punctual so that we do not lose any time with the breaks. So we will stick to this timetable, and we will be working four hours, as we did with our previous time schedule. So this is an attempt to reorganise our timetable in view of the circumstances. So without much further ado, we will continue with the testimony of General Krstic. General Krstic, I remind you that you are still under an oath. So we will work until quarter past ten. And when I say "quarter past ten," of course it can always be fourteen past ten or sixteen past ten. The counsel will tell us when it is the convenient time to have a break. Let me now give the floor to Mr. Petrusic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. President; good morning, Your Honours; good morning counsel for the Prosecution. The Defence should also like to bid good morning to everybody present in this courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. Petrusic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, yesterday you mentioned Zeleni Jadar, and you linked it with the documents that were presented to you and the Chamber. My next question is the following: At the beginning of June, was an operation conducted by the forces of the Drina Corps in the area of Zeleni Jadar? And I should like you to tell us something about that operation.

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After Srebrenica had been declared a safe area and after the boundaries of the safe area had been established, Zeleni Jadar, or to be more precise, one particular furniture factory located in Zeleni Jadar, remained outside the boundaries of the safe area; that is, it remained on the territory of Republika Srpska. That is the territory which was under the Serb control, which can be clearly seen from this map when looking at the initial positions of the Drina Corps in the Krivaja 95 operation. I am referring to this axis here. I am pointing at the Zeleni Jadar locality. The positions in question are behind Zeleni Jadar facing Srebrenica and further on the Bojna facilities. So these are the axes in question, and these are the forces deployed on their starting positions, so they were actually north of Zeleni Jadar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Zeleni Jadar is therefore behind the red lines which indicate the positions of the Drina Corps forces, that is, the VRS?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. The command of the armed formations of the BiH army even after the boundaries of the protected areas had been established, that is, those formations very often infiltrated themselves in the factory, whether it was with a view of carrying preparations for operations or to conduct operations from that particular locality. Very often, those formations took furniture and other fixtures from the factory. So the command of the Drina Corps, because of such a situation and also because of the security of its units in that particular portion of the frontage, the command was -- had to protect its units, and it also had to protect the property in question and prevent looting of the factory. Appropriate measures were taken to that -- in that respect, and after that the UNPROFOR command moved its checkpoint which used to be situated east of the factory. The new location of the checkpoint was behind the factory facilities, and the command of the Drina Corps didn't in any way prevent the UNPROFOR forces to carry out their assignments and their mission. This move cannot be interpreted as a violation of the Security Council resolution and the agreement that was signed between the warring factions by the VRS. The agreement in question was signed by General Mladic and the Chief of Staff of the BiH army, General Sefer Halilovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the attack, or rather, at the time of the attack and those military operations, or perhaps sometime before that, were elite units grouped, elite units of the Drina Corps or the VRS, were they grouped in the area around Zeleni Jadar at the time of that operation?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, I have to say that in view of the situation at the time and the period of time during which the VRS was acting, and also because of the ever-present danger of a breakthrough of front lines in the western part of the area of responsibility of the Drina Corps, that is, from the direction of Tuzla, Kladanj, and Zivinice, the Drina Corps command and the corps in general were not able to deploy any additional forces around the area of the Srebrenica and Zepa enclaves, so that's one of the reasons. The second reason was the fact that in the western part of Republika Srpska, the situation was very complex at the time, in particular in the area of responsibility of the 2nd Krajina Corps. The events that unfolded later on will prove that. The Drina Corps Command, therefore, was not in a position to deploy any additional forces to close the area from the direction of Srebrenica and Zepa. So around the protected area of Srebrenica, the remaining forces were those forces that had been there from earlier on, that is, the Bratunac Brigade, the Independent Skelani Battalion, the Milici Brigade. Of course, the combat readiness at the time was increased because of the offensive of the BH army that we thought might happen because of the information that we had at the time. The Drina Corps Command, acting pursuant to an order issued by the Main Staff, was forced to move one battalion from the Milici Brigade and to dispatch it to the area of responsibility of the 2nd Krajina Corps. The replenishment of that battalion was carried out by deploying elderly people who were not able to carry out any combat activities. Such units were only able to remain in trenches and on defensive lines. So those were the reasons that the Drina Corps Command and its units were not able to deploy any additional forces at that time, let alone elite units, and bring them around the area of the enclave.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In one of your previous responses regarding this issue, you indicated the area in question on the map, but technical conditions were not perfect, so I will try to clarify the issue through another question. The Bratunac and Milici Brigades and the Independent Skelani Battalion, were they still at their positions, the positions that they had taken up at the time the safe area was declared?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time Srebrenica was declared a safe area, those units were indeed on their positions which they had held from before, that is, before Srebrenica had been declared a protected area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, you are referring to the north-western part of the theatre and to the military operations that were taking part at that time in the area of responsibility of the Drina Corps. Could you tell us what was actually happening in the north-western part of your area of responsibility and what brigades and what units from your area of responsibility were engaged?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As part of the spring offensive of the BH army, on the 14th or, actually, the 15th of June, 1995, forces of the 2nd Corps of the BH army launched an offensive that had been planned before. The offensive in question was launched toward defensive lines of the Drina Corps, more precisely, in the north-western area of the Drina Corps area of responsibility. The attack was carried out along two axes. The main body of troops of the BH army, of the 2nd Corps, were grouped along the Tuzla-Zvornik axis, whereas the additional forces of the BH army were in the area of Kladanj-Vlasenica, along the Kladanj-Vlasenica axis. It was a synchronised attack, and it was directed against the 1st Bircanska Infantry Brigade and partially also against the 1st Zvornik Infantry Brigade but also against the positions of the 1st Vlasenica Infantry Brigade. After the initial successes, the forces of the 2nd Corps of the BH army and the loss of some of the territory on the Tuzla-Zvornik axis, to be more specific, in the area of the Kalesija municipality and the Osmaci municipality, the offensive launched by the 2nd Corps of the BH army was stopped. On that occasion, the Drina Corps forces, in particular along the Tuzla-Zvornik axis, again to be more specific, the forces of the 1st Bircanska Brigade and also part of the 1st Zvornik Brigade, did suffer some casualties. So this offensive lasted for two days, and after the regrouping of the forces within the two brigades that I have just mentioned and the introduction of the new forces from the area of responsibility of the Drina Corps which had not come under the attack or were attacked by a smaller body of troops, we managed after stopping the offensive to repel the forces of the 2nd Corps of the BiH army to their initial positions. So this was the beginning of the offensive launched by the forces of the BiH army on the 15th and the -- in fact, the 14th and the 15th of June, 1995.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't have to use the map any more.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would now like to ask the usher to remove the map from the ELMO that's Prosecution Exhibit number 2, and to place Defence Exhibit 127 on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this is Exhibit 127, a report of the Drina Corps command, number is 15-354/32, dated 15th of June, 1995. It is entitled "Report About the Combat Situation in the Drina Corps Area," and it is this dispatch submitted to all the subordinate units by the commander, Major General Milenko Zivanovic. General, can you tell us something about this report?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a report filed by the commander of the Drina Corps, General Zivanovic, to all his subordinate commanders within the corps. This report shows that the Drina Corps Commander notifies his subordinate commanders about the fact that the spring offensive of the BiH army is at its peak, and that the forces of the Republika Srpska army managed in all sections of the front to stop the forces of the BiH army, and in some cases, they created conditions for launching counter-attacks. At the same time, he advises them that the BiH army has not ceased with its attacks on the area of responsibility of the Drina Corps, and as I have already stated, you can see that from this report, that an offensive has been launched against the Drina Corps by the 2nd Corps of the BiH army. He further advises them that as part of this offensive launched by the 2nd Corps, there is a simultaneous activity launched from the safe areas of Srebrenica and Zepa against Drina Corps forces within its area of responsibility. He also notifies them of the fact that the forces of the 2nd Corps of the BiH army in the first stage of the operation, or rather, the offensive, did achieve some success, but that the forces of the Drina Corps have managed to hold the offensive successfully. So the assessments of the Drina Corps Commander and of the subordinate commands were correct, in fact, and the assessment was that the BiH army, or to be more specific, its 2nd Corps, would also be engaged in the spring offensive attacking both the positions of the Drina Corps in the northwestern part of the corps area of responsibility. In crushing the second stage of the operation launched -- I apologise -- of the first stage of the offensive launched by the BiH army, the command was forced to regroup its forces in order to halt this offensive and to crush the offensive and to push the forces of the 2nd Corps to their initial positions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Our next exhibit is Exhibit 88 issued by the Drina Corps command. Its number is 94/67-3 -- 94/76-3, dated 19th of June, 1995, issued by the commander of the Corps, Major General Zivanovic. General, is this document in a way a result of the report, or how do you interpret the order issued as part of this document?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely. This report is related to or deals with the initial stages of the offensive launched by the 2nd Corps of the BiH army against the area of responsibility of the corps. In particular, in this report the commander of the Drina Corps stresses and warns his subordinate commanders about the fact that from the safe areas of Srebrenica and Zepa and Gorazde, extremely strong forces are being infiltrated into the area of responsibility of the Corps, more specifically, behind the forces that are engaged in the defence. He provides an example of that in the direction of the Gorazde enclave when the forces of the 8th Division from Gorazde infiltrated their forces in behind the lines of the 1st Podrinje Light Infantry Brigade, on which occasion they inflicted enormous casualties on them. We have information that the forces of the 28th Division from Srebrenica, after the beginning of the attack which was launched from the direction of Tuzla, that they were infiltrated into the wider region of Udrc and Cerska, waiting to be linked up with the forces attacking along the Tuzla-Zvornik axis. We did touch upon that yesterday. I said something about it when I explained the documents of the BH army related to the tasks assigned to the 28th Division in the course of the offensive launched by the 2nd Corps of the BH army.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Document 89. This is a document issued by the Command of the 1st Milici Brigade, and the number it bears is Roman numeral I/01-617-1. It is dated the 19th of June, 1995. It is signed by the Commander of the brigade, Captain First Class Milomir Nastic. The document is entitled: "The Activities of the Reconnaissance and Terrorist Groups of the Enemy, Intelligence Report."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Milici Brigade was around the area, the safe area of Srebrenica, and it was a subordinate brigade, brigade that was subordinate to the Drina Corps. I should like to ask you to comment on this document.

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Milici Brigade was engaged in the defence of the area west of the safe area of Srebrenica. This report was written by the Commander of the Milici Brigade, and he sent it to all his subordinate units within the brigade. This report primarily deals with the activities of the 28th Division, which is carrying out reconnaissance and sabotage activities against the positions of his brigade and deep behind the lines Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. of the brigade. In this report, he also mentions the activities of the 28th Division, which at that time was carrying out reconnaissance, sabotage, and terrorist activities within the area of responsibility of the Bratunac Brigade and of the Skelani Independent Battalion. He warns his subordinates about the fact that the forces of the 28th Division are making good use of the status, in inverted commas, safe area, and "pass through our undefended and intermediate areas with no problems at all, carrying out reconnaissance actions and infiltrating sabotage and terrorist groups which inflict great losses upon the other forces."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is the 19th of June that we are talking about. What was the situation like in the north-western area of your corps' area of responsibility had it been stabilised?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It is indeed the 19th of June, 1995, and as I have already said, the forces of the Drina Corps had managed to halt the offensive of the 2nd Corps of the BH army to stabilise its defensives and to restore lost territory, restore control over the lost territory. The activities of the 28th Division continue uninterruptedly before the offensive and during the offensive.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The next exhibit is Exhibit number 90. This is a regular combat report of the Command of the 1st Bircani [Realtime transcript omitted "Bircani"] Brigade. The number is 03/1 -- sorry -- 03/1-691, dated the 21st of June, 1995. So it is a regular combat report to the Command of the Drina Corps, signed by Commander Colonel Svetozar Andric.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is this report by Colonel Andric informing the Corps Command about?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I apologise, but in the transcript it says the "1st Brigade" but not the "1st Bircani Brigade."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We've corrected it now. It is indeed the document issued by the Command of the 1st Bircani Infantry Brigade. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please continue, General.

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Command of the Drina Corps had correctly assessed that the forces of the 2nd Corps of the BH army would not give up their intention of re-launching the offensive or, rather, of continuing it. So on the 21st of June, once again along the Tuzla-Zvornik axis, they carried out synchronised attacks against the positions of the 1st Bircani Brigade, partly the Vlasenica Brigade, and partly the Zvornik Brigade. In this report, the Brigade Commander informs the Corps Command that an attack has been launched, that the attack is an extremely powerful one, that very large infantry units were engaged in the attack, of course, supported by artillery and other logistic support. He also informs the Command of the Drina Corps that in this renewed offensive or, rather, the continuation of the offensive, the forces of the 2nd Corps of the BH army, in view of the circumstances, were extremely successful. After having in the area of Kalesija, Bis, the territory of the Serbian municipality of Osmaci, having formed a bridgehead on the Spreca River, they managed to gain control of the village of Vukovina, the village of Markovici, the larger area of the village of Osmaci, the village of Zelena. These mentioned villages were burned down, inflicting civilian casualties, and the Brigade Commander reports that in his brigade -- this is the Commander of the Bircani Brigade -- reports to his superiors that he is having casualties but he does not know exactly how many dead or wounded. We will see later on that after this offensive was crushed, the forces of the Drina Corps, or more specifically, the 1st Bircani Brigade, had about 120 dead and wounded combatants. The offensive went on round the clock, day and night, until the 26th of June when forces of the Drina Corps, holding defensive positions and forces being brought in from other parts of the Drina Corps front, and also some other forces from the areas of responsibility of other corps, we managed to halt and repel this offensive. That was how on the 26th we managed to thwart the offensive, push back the forces of the 2nd Corps to their initial positions. We had information at the time, and this could be seen from the relevant documents of the BiH army, that the forces of the 28th Division from Srebrenica took an active part in the offensive activities launched from the Tuzla axis. Before the beginning of this offensive, the forces of one infantry battalion strength were transferred systematically from Srebrenica, and their commander was General Naser Oric. At the same time, units of the 28th Division throughout the renewed offensive engaged in reconnaissance and sabotage and terrorist activities in the first place behind the lines of the Milici Brigade west of the safe area of Srebrenica, and also towards the territory of the municipality of Han Pijesak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is fine, General. In the meantime, that is, during the period we were discussing and the events you described for us, where were you situated?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Throughout the duration of the operation, that is, from the 14th of June until the offensive was crushed on the 26th of June, I was within the area of responsibility of the 1st Bircani Brigade, that is, on the forward command post of this brigade in the village of Osmaci where, together with the other officers, and I have in mind in the first place the commander of the 1st Bircani Brigade and the 1st Zvornik Brigade as well as of another officer from the commander of the Drina Corps, that is, Colonel Milanovic, I monitored the combat operations. Together with the commander of the 1st Bircani and 1st Zvornik Brigades, I undertook measures to halt the offensive of the 2nd Corps of the BiH army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Petrusic, would this be a good moment for the break? So please look at your watches now, and come back in a quarter of an hour, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Registrar is not here yet, but I think we can still proceed. Mr. Petrusic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, you went back from the area of the Bircani Brigade to your command post in Vlasenica; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I should like the Exhibit 91 to be presented at this point.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This exhibit is an interim combat report issued by the command of the 1st Bratunac Brigade, number 03-253-82/1, dated 23rd of June, 1995. The document is signed by the commander, Colonel Vidoje Blagojevic. Did this interim combat report reach the command post in Vlasenica, and what was the issue that Colonel Blagojevic wanted to notify you of in this document?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After I had come back to the command post, from the forward command post of the 1st Bircani Brigade --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Visnjic, is there a problem?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, there is a discrepancy in Exhibit 91A and 91B. I'm sure that it is a mistake in translation. In the heading of the document 91B in the original, it is stated, "Command of the 1st," and then there is an abbreviation which means the Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade. However, this acronym was translated into English the "1st Bircanska Light Infantry Brigade." It should be corrected. The brigade in question is actually the 1st Bratunac Brigade which was commanded by Vidoje Blagojevic. I just wanted to draw your attention to this mistake in translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. Visnjic. I have also noticed this discrepancy which will have to be corrected. Bircanska will have to become Bratunac, the 1st Bratunac Brigade. Thank you. Mr. Petrusic, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, I should like to know whether you are familiar with this report, and whether the command of the corps was notified of this report, and what the report is all about.

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After I had come back from the forward command post of the 1st Bircanska Brigade, that is from the area of Osmaci to the command post in Vlasenica, I was briefed on a number of documents of this kind, like this combat report that we have here which was submitted by the commander of the 1st Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade. Throughout the time of this offensive, the 28th Division was very active towards our defensive lines in Srebrenica, around Srebrenica, and also by infiltrating themselves into the depth of our territory around the enclave. As regards this particular report, the Commander of the 1st Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade is informing the Drina Corps Command about one particular operation which was carried out by the members of the 28th Division against his positions. In this report, he makes mention of the losses he sustained in the operation. One soldier was killed, a member of his brigade, of a unit which was deployed in the area where this incident took place.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Our next exhibit is document number 92. This document is also a report of the Bratunac Brigade and bears the number 02/415-1, dated 24th of June, 1995. The document again was issued by Vidoje Blagojevic. The situation is the same as the one described in the previous document; that is, again, we have a mistake in translation. The English version reads the "1st Bircani Brigade" but the signature is the same in both documents, that is, the signature of the Commander, Vidoje Blagojevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, these two reports follow one another day after day. Could you tell us something about the contents of this other document, document number 92, and what this document is all about.

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document is another document in the series of reports to the Drina Corps Command to its subordinate units whereby the Command of the corps is informed of the activities of the 28th Division from Srebrenica. The commander of this brigade is informing the Drina Corps Command about the fact that in the past previous days, the 28th Division did not engage in major operations against the positions of his brigade. However, he learned that from the headquarters, and he's probably referring to the General Staff of the BH army, an order was issued to emphasise sabotage and terrorist activities and to continue with the infiltration of such groups, that is, to focus on infiltration activities, and that with such activities, the objective can be reached in the most efficient way while incurring major losses within the enemy forces and causing panic amongst the enemy forces both with the members of the Drina Corps units and also amongst the population living in the area of responsibility of the Drina Corps, that is, in the theatre of these operations. The Commander of the 1st Bratunac Brigade, in this report, gives a number of examples of the activities conducted by the 28th Division, the way you described, day by day, day after day. He states localities where the infiltrations took place, and he also indicates the strength of the infiltrating units as well as the result and the effect of their operations. I should just like to draw your attention to the second example that is given in this report involving what took place on the 23rd of June. It says that in the area of the Osmaca village, which is on the road to Zeleni Jadar, on the same day at about 17.30, they infiltrated a group of their soldiers and laid an ambush in which they killed four members of the MUP of Republika Srpska who were returning from a mission. Actually, there had been a rotation at the checkpoint near the Zeleni Jadar factory, and that locality was actually under the control of the MUP forces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This report and the previous report were sent at the time while the operation and combat activities were still ongoing in the north-western area of responsibility of the Drina Corps, that is, the area of responsibility of the Bircani Brigade.

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The forces of the 28th Division, in this period of time, were conducting the assignments of the Skakavac operation, but they were also actively involved in these type of activities, cooperating with the forces acting from the direction of Tuzla. Those forces were attacking along the Tuzla-Zvornik axis towards the area of Podrinje and Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned on several occasions, both today and yesterday, that Skakavac operation. What was the final objective of that operation?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This operation was carried out by the forces of the BiH army. The very name of the operation Skakavac, or meaning grasshopper in English, is symbolic and has to do with the way the operations were conducted. And the way the assignments were being carried out, the idea was to conduct as many terrorist activities as possible throughout the area which was under the control of the VRS, that is, on the territory controlled by Serbs. In this way, by carrying out the assignments that were part of this operation, the forces of the 28th Division were participating in a most direct way in the attack which was also carried out by the forces attacking from the Tuzla-Kladanj axis, from that direction.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During that period of time and also before that, that is, during the combat activities around the area of Zeleni Jadar at the beginning of June, did you and your command engage in the preparations for the Krivaja 95 operation; and the activities that were going on around the area of the Zeleni Jadar that were conducted by the members of the Drina Corps, were they some kind of introduction to the preparatory phase of the Krivaja 95 operation?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In view of the situation that the command of the Drina Corps found itself in, as well as its units, and that was the period of the preparations for and implementation of the spring offensive against the area of responsibility of the Drina Corps, and in view of the activities of the 28th Division from safe areas, I wish to state with full responsibility that in the command of the Drina Corps, no one in those days, before those days and at that time, had any plan for an attack against Srebrenica. Regarding activities carried out at the beginning of June in the area of Zeleni Jadar, I would describe those operations as lawful operations and measures taken by the Drina Corps to protect its units in this segment of the front from the activities of the 28th Division, and to protect the property of the Zeleni Jadar factory. Under no circumstances did we by those activities violate the provisions of the United Nations resolution in relation to the safe area.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One more exhibit, please, D93. It is an interim combat report of the 1st Milici Light Infantry Brigade, number 332-1684, dated the 26th of June, 1995. The report is from Milomir Nastic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This interim combat report coincides with the period when the offensive was being thwarted in the northwestern part of the theatre of the area of responsibility of the Drina Corps. So, the date is the 26th of June, 1995, and the report relates to the activities of enemy units engaged in from the safe area. Could you comment, please, and give us your interpretation of this combat report which was addressed to the command of the Drina Corps on the 26th of June.

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the period when the offensive was still ongoing and was being repulsed, the offensive by the 2nd Corps of the BiH army. The 28th Division, however, was still extremely active in sabotage and terrorist activities in the rear of the lines of our units deployed towards Srebrenica and Zepa. This report of the 26th of June in which the commander, or rather, Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. his representative of the 1st Milici Brigade, informs the command of the Drina Corps that the forces of the 28th Division which had spent some time in the area of Radava, as I was describing yesterday, via a feature called Kupusna which is located within Vlasenica municipality, they entered the village of Visnjica, carried out an act of sabotage there, and in the attack on this village and the positions around the village, they killed one soldier from his brigade. Then they attacked the village, inflicted losses among the civilian population, torched the village, and then withdrew from the area. I spoke about this yesterday when I testified about the documents of the BiH army that we have in our possession. On that same day -- and I also testified about that yesterday -- from this same area of Radava, the broader area of the Main Staff of the army of Republika Srpska was attacked from the east, and on that occasion, six soldiers who were providing security of the Main Staff were killed and a number of them wounded. On that same day also, those same forces continued their operations and attacked the village of Rjecice in the municipality of Han Pijesak, where they killed ten civilians and torched the remaining houses which had not been burnt down during the operations in 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the offensive was crushed or, rather, at the end of combat operations in the area of responsibility of the Bircani Brigade, did that brigade and the Corps Command engage in certain activities to reclaim and clean up the theatre in the areas of Osmaci and other places that you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Drina Corps Command and the Command of the 1st Bircani Infantry Brigade and the 1st Zvornik Infantry Brigade had the duty or were in a situation when they urgently had to put some order in these two brigades, the focus being on the 1st Bircani Infantry Brigade. What this means is stabilising the front lines, removing the consequences of the operations by the 2nd Corps of the BH army to clean up the areas in which battles were conducted, as well as in the villages which had been captured by the 2nd Corps of the BH army. I personally was assigned the task by the Commander of the Drina Corps to carry out these activities that I have just described, as soon as possible. So he gave me orders that at the Vis feature a facility be built and as a forward command post for the Drina Corps within the area of responsibility of the 1st Bircani Brigade because there was the danger of this offensive being repeated. I was also tasked to repair damaged roads, roads that had been damaged during these operations, and if necessary, to build new roads to facilitate supplies and evacuations. As soon as I received these orders from the Corps Command, I called the Commander of the 5th Engineers Battalion, giving him specific assignments in this regard. The Command of the 5th Engineers Battalion accepted those orders and took steps to carry them out immediately, and he completed all these activities in the course of the month of August.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us briefly comment further on this particular date, the 26th of June.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Exhibit number 94, please. It is a regular combat report, number 03-253-86 of the 26th of June, 1995, signed by Vidoje Blagojevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the heading of this document, we do not have the name of the brigade, but in view of the signatory, General, would this be a report of the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, Mr. President. Microphone. Microphone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me. Is there a discrepancy again that you wish to attract our attention to?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. On the original document the number is 03-253-86, but the translator said 03-253-85. So this last number differs between the original and the English text. But I think that the mistake is in the original, in view of the order in which the documents have been marked. So strictly speaking, the translation differs from the original.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So we will take note of it and make the correction. My translation that I received was that this was a Prosecution Exhibit. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Never mind. But that was the interpretation I received, and I was a bit confused. But please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, first of all, is this a document issued by the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. You can see that from the signature which is at the bottom of this document, indicating that it is the Commander, Colonel Vidoje Blagojevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does this regular combat report indicate -- can it be concluded on its basis that the activities continue, that the enemy operations in the area of the Zvornik Brigade, that they continue?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In paragraph 1 of this report, the operations of the 28th Division against some parts of the positions of this brigade are discussed, so this is not the infiltration but the operations launched from the safe area against the positions of the brigade. More specifically, he states the area, the section of the positions from which his forces came under an attack, that is to the north of Buljim. I apologise, of Buljim.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were members of the 5th Engineer Battalion also engaged in this area? I mean the engineer battalion of the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the area of responsibility of the Bratunac Brigade, or more specifically, on its positions to the east of the safe area, mention is made of the engagement of the forces of the 5th Engineer Battalion. I have already spoken about the use of this battalion, explaining the documents of the army of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. These were their reports in which they indicated that they had noticed the construction machinery at work to the east of the enclave. This Caus facility, more specifically, the positions of the Bratunac Brigade, were fortified, or the fortifications were reinforced on the Caus facility. As I said yesterday, there was no need to fortify your positions if you were planning an attack, or at least, not to such an extent that you would need to engage construction machinery. And on this occasion, the road and bridge construction company of the engineer battalion was engaged, and they were located in Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would now like to go on to the planning of the operation Krivaja 95. As you have already said on several occasions, you were aware of the Security Council resolution as regards the establishment of the safe areas of Srebrenica and Zepa.

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was aware of the Security Council resolution establishing Srebrenica and Zepa as safe areas.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You spoke about the demilitarisation agreement, and we really do not need to go back to that, but were the units of the Drina Corps that were deployed around the Srebrenica safe area in compliance with the Security Council UN resolution indicating that the safe areas should not be attacked?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, because I was absent for a longer period of time after taking over the post of the Chief of Staff, and I did not spend a long time in the Corps command even thereafter. There are no examples of the 1st Bratunac and Milici Brigades and the independent Skelani Battalion that were deployed around the safe area of Srebrenica, that they violated the UN Security Council resolution. There are no examples so far of any -- not a single instance when any of these units entered into that safe area. If there were some activities launched from the front lines, from the defence lines, then it was only carried out in response to the fire being opened by the 28th Division against their positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would now like the Exhibit 74 to be placed on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The heading of this document indicates the following: Military postal code; and the number is 161-1; date, 14th of March, 1995; Milici; and it is unsigned. You were aware of the military structure and organisation that existed within the zone of the Muslim forces.

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was, primarily from the intelligence, the ones that I received either from the subordinate units or from the intelligence organ of the Drina Corps command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this -- the intelligence about their structure contained in this exhibit?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is the intelligence, the data, but from the time period when the forces of the BiH army in the safe areas of Srebrenica and Zepa were organised as part of the 8th Operative Group, from mid-1994 until the May of 1995. I spoke about the restructuring, the strong restructuring and the reestablishment of the units of the 28th Division, and in this process, they became larger. So this formation in the safe area had 5.000 -- had, I apologise, had five brigades. At the time when the units of the BiH army in the safe areas were organised as the 8th Operative Group, the 8th Operative Group had five brigades, and all of them were deployed in the safe area of Srebrenica. Also as part of the 8th Operative Group, in addition to the five brigades, there was also the independent battalion composed of the crack troops from the area. The commander of the forces of the 8th Operative Group was Naser Oric, and later after the 8th Operative Group was restructured to become the 28th infantry division.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: According to your estimate, or rather, the estimate of the Drina Corps command or the relevant organs, how many soldiers, active soldiers of military age were involved in these brigades?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The data obtained from the intelligence organ of the 1st Milici Light Infantry Brigade referring to the strength of each of the brigades, I would say that they are indeed correct, so that we can draw the conclusion that the 8th Operative Group at the time when it existed as the 8th Operative Group numbered about 6.000 soldiers. However, later when the 8th Operative Group was restructured as the 28th Division, their strength changed considerably so that each brigade had between 1.000 and 1.800 soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, I suggest we make a break now, and we can continue at 11.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, very well. Thank you very much. We are now going to have another 15-minute break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Petrusic, you may continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, I should like to know something about the structure of the weapons that the units which were concentrated in the protected area had. I'm referring to the units of the 28th Division or the 8th Operative Group.

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From this report, which among other things provides information about the type of weapons which the units of the 28th Division had, were armed with, one can see that the said units were armed with light infantry weapons or, rather, infantry weapons, which should also include weapons for combat at close encounters, such as Zoljas and Osas, the hand-held rocket launchers, then hand-held rocket launchers M57, then mortars of 60 millimetre calibre. They also had anti-aircraft weapons whose calibre was 20 millimetres. One can see here that some heavy weapons were also used by this division. Mention is made of a howitzer which was concealed or, rather, dug in somewhere inside the protected area of Srebrenica. I should, however, stress that the units of the 8th Operative Group, when it comes to their further organisation in terms of formations according to establishment, were additionally armed, received additional weapons. And this is something that I spoke about yesterday and the day before when I said that weapons were being brought into the area from the direction of Tuzla and Kladanj. On one occasion, I interpreted one of the documents of the BH army, and I noted that they had 120 millimetre mortars as well. Those units were additionally armed with infantry weapons, as the units of the 28th Division were growing in strength. And the 8th Operative Group was renamed 28th Division at the beginning of May 1995. At that time, apart from the Division Command, it also had headquarters units, staff units, and an independent battalion which consisted of elite units from that area. The division also had five -- that is, six brigades which were located inside the protected area, and one such brigade was located in the area of the Zepa protected zone. After the 8th Operative Group was renamed the 28th Division, that particular unit, the unit of that type of organisation and structure, was organised according to the principles of structuring and organising of such units in the former Yugoslav People's Army, so that the strength of the brigades was between 1.000 to 1.800 troops. So altogether, the division could have be somewhere between 6.000 and 10.000 members who were armed, who had been armed as members of the 8th Operative Brigade and continued to be armed as members of the 28th Division.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For the record, can we just conclude that there were five brigades altogether?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Srebrenica as part of the 8th Operative Group, there were five brigades during that period of time. Later on when the 8th Operative Group was renamed 28th Division, there were five brigades in Srebrenica, plus one independent battalion, and one additional brigade which was located in Zepa.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I should like to have the exhibit number 33 put on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We spoke about this particular exhibit yesterday, and I should like to ask you to tell us briefly whether the information that you had, that your command had obtained as regards the organisational structure of the 8th Operative Group and later the 28th Division, so I'm referring both to the organisation of the unit and the types of weapons that they had, so whether according to that information the two units, the 8th Operative Group and the 28th Division, were similar in type in terms of strength and organisation and weapons?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to what we received from the intelligence department of the 1st Milici Brigade and when we compared their report with this particular exhibit, it was obvious that the 8th Operative Group was organised as -- in a way described in this document that we have previously seen. So there were five brigades in Srebrenica, and there was one independent mountain battalion. The brigades are the 28th East Bosnian Brigade, 281st East Bosnian Light Brigade, 282nd East Bosnian Light Brigade, and 283rd East Bosnian Light Brigade, 284th East Bosnian Light Brigade, and one independent battalion, mountain battalion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, could you tell us something about how you and the Drina Corps command came to the decision to plan the Krivaja 95 operation, and how a decision was made to attack Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So far I have spoken about the intentions, objectives, and specific measures that were undertaken in respect of the spring offensive of the BiH army, the main objective being, let me repeat, the linking up of the protected areas with the territory of Tuzla, Zivinice, and Kladanj. However, what is far more important and what should be emphasised is the fact that Srebrenica, like Zepa, were never really demilitarised. There was a large amount of military-able men and troops that were organised in five or six brigades. The brigades were constantly conducting combat operations against the positions of the Drina Corps area Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. around the protected area of Srebrenica and also deep behind the lines of these units, and such attacks resulted in major losses for us, losses involving both our troops, and also one has to bear in mind that it caused considerable panic among [Realtime transcript read in error "Monday"] the civilian population. So the Drina Corps command for those reasons could no longer tolerate this behaviour, and it decided to undertake an operation whose secret code name was Krivaja 95. So this operation began both in terms of preparations and plans, was caused by the situation in the territory where the members of the 28th Division were particularly active.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Petrusic. Mr. Visnjic, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, page 30, line 20, the word that we can see on the transcript is "Monday," and I don't think that it was mentioned. The word should probably be "amongst" the civilian population.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, thank you, Mr. Visnjic, but I think that it's one of the mistakes that are corrected on a regular basis by the typists later on. Of course, no mention was made of "Monday." I'm sure that the typist will be able to correct the mistake. Mr. Petrusic, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, did you and the command of the Drina Corps become familiar with the directives number 7 and 7/1, directive 7 having been issued by the Supreme Commander of the armed forces of Republika Srpska, and directive 7/1 which was issued by the Main Staff of the VRS?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The Drina Corps Command knew about those directives that were issued by the Supreme Command of Republika Srpska and the Main Staff of the VRS. The directives in question are directive number 7 and directive number 7/1. In these directives, the Drina Corps Command had -- these directives constituted a formal basis for the Drina Corps Command to plan and conduct an operation of this kind. However, I have already mentioned the main reasons which governed the decision of the Drina Corps Command to plan and implement this type of operation. In directives number 7 and number 7/1, specific assignments or, rather, general assignments were given to all units of the VRS, including the Drina Corps, and the directives also made mention of the type of activities that had to be taken around the protected areas.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the basis of what did you or, rather, the command make the decision to plan and carry out the operation Krivaja?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Naturally, the Drina Corps Command, in spite of these two directives and in spite of the situation in the area that I have described at length, could not make such a decision independently. The Command of the Drina Corps was given an oral order from the commander of the Main Staff immediately to prepare and carry out this operation, being guided exclusively by all the developments in the safe areas which climaxed, I would say, on the 26th of June when units of the 28th Division broke into the villages of Visnjica and Rjecice, and when they attacked the Main Staff from the direction of Banja Lucica and Krivace.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the main idea of the Corps Commander?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The basic concept of the Drina Corps Commander, which would later be translated into a decision, was exclusively to separate the two enclaves, Srebrenica and Zepa.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have Prosecution Exhibit 427, please. That's fine. Thank you. It is the preparatory order number 1 of the Drina Corps Command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was your response to the order or notification in view of the concept of the commander to separate the two enclaves, Srebrenica and Zepa, and what did you actually do?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As soon as the commander of the Drina Corps, General Zivanovic, returned from the Main Staff, and that happened on the 2nd of July, 1995, he convened his assistants -- and I was one of them as the Chief of Staff and his deputy -- and he told us what was the assignment given to him by the Commander of the Main Staff, saying that we must urgently prepare and carry out the operation Krivaja 95. And on that occasion, a very brief assessment was made of everything that was happening at the time in the north-western part of the corps area of responsibility and also within the area of responsibility of the Drina Corps, and I am referring primarily to the activities of the 28th Division, saying simply that the area between the Srebrenica and Zepa enclaves has to be placed under control. After making a brief overview of the situation and of the measures taken by the BH army against the area of responsibility of the Drina Corps and within that area, the commander conveyed his concept, his idea, and that was to separate Srebrenica and Zepa. To that end and prior to the elaboration of all the necessary documents for such an operation, which was planned to last a very short time, he issued these preparatory orders to subordinate units which were to take part in the execution of his main idea or decision.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the key aim of this preparatory order?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The substance of that order is to give commanders a very brief assessment of everything that had taken place until then in relation to the area of responsibility and within the area of responsibility of the Drina Corps. In other words, for the brigade commanders to be reminded once again, though all this was still fresh in their minds, these operations were still ongoing. The very substance of this preparatory order was for the brigade commanders who received that preparatory order to assess the situation in their respective areas of responsibility and to set aside a part of the forces which would take part in the execution of his concept or decision. I said to make an assessment because the situation in the area of responsibility and around it was still extremely complicated and there was a danger that the offensive from Tuzla and Kladanj, and also from Olovo even, would be renewed and continued, and we had certain information to that effect.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the Corps Commander tasks his subordinate units from among their forces to detach a certain number of units that would take part in the execution of a future task. Does he define that task in this order?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The Corps Commander, in this preparatory order, does not define the task within the framework of Krivaja 95. The detachment of forces from these brigades could have been used along other axes, because the situation, as I have said, was extremely, extremely complex. The brigade commanders who did not know where their forces would be deployed embarked upon the implementation of this preparatory order by the Corps Commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was your role as the Chief of Staff in the implementation and execution of this preparatory order?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My role and tasks as the Chief of Staff of the Drina Corps are prescribed by the regulations on the work of commands and staffs, also the regulations of the land forces, and other documents. In this particular case, my role was to assist the brigade commanders, and that was the duty not only of me but the other assistant commanders, for the segment of the forces to be pulled out from the front so that this preparatory order could be implemented. After ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Corps Commander, did he consult with you and other assistant commanders regarding the strength of the forces that needed to be deployed for this decision to be carried out?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is regulated by our rules and regulations, by the rules of combat governing warfare and the conduct of operations. If the Corps Commander could do that on his own, then he wouldn't need assistants, any one of those assistants. When it comes to this particular situation and his decision or his main idea to separate the enclaves of Srebrenica and Zepa, the commander did not really need to consult with his assistants and with me specifically as the Chief of Staff and his deputy because ever since the formation of the Corps, he had been the Corps Commander. He comes from the territory of Srebrenica municipality. He was frequently in the area. He was familiar with the situation within the safe areas. He had information on the organisation and structure of the 28th Division, their intentions, their aims, and throughout this time he was fully briefed on what was happening and what measures had been taken by the 28th Division in relation to the Drina Corps. He was also very well informed about our own forces that were deployed around the safe area of Srebrenica. These were the 1st Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade, the 1st Milici Light Infantry Brigade, and the Skelani Independent Battalion. In addition to this knowledge, the commander also knew what their capacities were in terms of combat, and I'm referring in the first place to their ability to take part in offensive action in order to implement this decision of his. But in spite of the fact that he was familiar with all these things, he did want to hear the opinion of his assistants, and they only confirmed what he already knew when making an assessment as to the strength of the forces that needed to be engaged to carry out this operation of separating Srebrenica from Zepa.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you participate with the commanders of the subordinate units in making the assessments as to the forces which could be pulled from the front of the -- held by the subordinate units without upsetting the balance of power, balance of power at the front and causing problems in this respect?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is a very important question. I did take part, together with the commanders who received the preparatory order, in the assessment and the possibility of detaching these forces for the execution of the task, knowing, just as they did, that it would not be easy; in particular, because there were grounds for concern, and the assessments indicated that the offensive in the northwest part of the area of responsibility of the corps could be repeated, renewed. In the course of making the assessment together with them, we were not optimistic, I would say, when it came to detaching these forces, but we did believe that we would execute the mission very soon and that we would be able to return the detached forces to their original units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After this preparatory order was issued and this whole process that you just talked about was completed, what was the next step taken by the Drina Corps command in the implementation of the preparatory order?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, after the assessments were made and the units were inspected by the command organs, the corps command organs, on the 2nd of July, 1995, in the afternoon, the Drina Corps Commander, General Zivanovic, formed a group that was to carry out the command reconnaissance at the corps command level. This group consisted of the Drina Corps Commander, General Zivanovic; myself as the Chief of Staff; then there was the chief of the operations and training section, Colonel Micic; then the chief of the intelligence section, Lieutenant Colonel Kosoric; chief of the communications in the Drina Corps, Lieutenant Colonel Blagojevic; and there was one of the commanding officers from the logistic organ of the Drina Corps, I think it was Lieutenant Colonel Jewicki, Henirik Jewicki. So after this group was formed, we went to the area in which combat operations would be conducted with the Corps Commander. We conducted the reconnaissance, from two points. One point -- I apologise, from three points. One was Pribicevac. That was the forward command post of the Pribicevac tactical group. The second point was Besica Brdo. The second point was Besica Brdo. This was the area here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the first point.

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first was the Pribicevac area, the second one was Besica Brdo, and the third one was the area of Bracani. After we conducted the command reconnaissance at the Drina Corps command level and verified what the commander of the corps had issued to the subordinate units in his preparatory order, I mean the strength and the forces that are to be engaged in the execution of this task, we went back to the command post in Vlasenica and continued our work on the preparation for the execution of this task.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So all these activities were part of the preparatory order?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely. All these activities of the Drina Corps command, the involvement of the Drina Corps command and their activities, were connected to the preparatory order issued by the Corps Commander and his basic concept that he communicated to us. But only after the command responsibility was the final decision of the Corps Commander made, and he issued specific tasks to his subordinate units, and all the other issues related to that were solved.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I please have the Prosecution Exhibit 428 placed on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After that, the Commander's decision was issued. Is this decision the order for active combat activities?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely. This is the order for active command activities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, could you please explain to us what is the meaning of this document, in fact, who issues the document, who takes part in it, all that is relevant for the issuing of such a document? Of course, I asked several questions as part of the single question, but let us answer them one by one.

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document is the order for active combat activities or, in other words, this is the decision of the Drina Corps Commander for the implementation of his basic concept that I have spoken about earlier.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Item 1 in this order contains the information about the enemy.

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This was the usual practice as regulated by the manual when it comes to the drafting of this document and similar documents about the execution of combat activities. Item 1 is the item containing information about the enemy, the assessment of his intentions, objectives, what the enemy had been doing in a certain period, what the enemy's doing now, and what the enemy intends to do. If you will allow me, I would like to read this item and explain parts of this item. The first portion of item 1 refers to the general assessment of the enemy, stating -- the enemy, unfortunately, I have to say, and the term is used to refer to the forces of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina: "As part of an all-out offensive against the army of the Republika Srpska carried out attacks with the limited objective against the Drina Corps units. We believe," that is, the text continues, "that in the coming period, the enemy will intensify offensive activities against the area of responsibility of the Drina Corps, mainly in the Tuzla-Zvornik and Kladanj-Vlasenica directions, with simultaneous activity by the 28th Division from the enclaves of Srebrenica and Zepa, in order to cut the area of the Drina Corps in two and to connect the enclaves with the central part of the territory of former Bosnia and Herzegovina."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, I'm sorry to be interrupting you. I think that the Trial Chamber has shown a great deal of understanding in setting our schedule for today, and I would like to suggest that we have our break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Petrusic. I hope I have understood you correctly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, you have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps we could go a little faster. It's true that I do not wish to give you any instructions regarding the conduct of your case -- it is up to you -- but if we have a document and if we have a translation of that document, surely it is not necessary to read it and repeat it. I understand that there is a case that you wish to present, and then in that context, you could put questions to General Krstic to refer to this document or to make an explanation, if necessary. I'm just making this observation to avoid any further loss of time. In any event, we are now going to have a 15-minute break. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Petrusic, you may continue. We will work until quarter past twelve, and after that we will have a one-hour break.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have to apologise, Mr. President, for this delay. The Defence didn't understand you correctly, so it is our mistake.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, in view of the order of the commander for active military activities and pursuant to that order, you give an assessment of the situation and the deployment of enemy forces. We are not going to comment on the document in detail, but please tell us briefly about it.

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As regards the first part of the order, the first item of the order of the Drina Corps Commander, I can say that the basic elements were given concerning the intentions and objectives, further intentions and objectives, of the BiH army forces towards the area of responsibility of the Drina Corps and inside that area of responsibility itself. I should say that this was known to the commanders of subordinate units; however, while drafting such documents, one must include these elements as well, this particular data, so that the units can be prepared in the best possible way for the execution of the assignment. Further on, the Corps Commander gives the essential data, the essential information about the forces inside the protected area of Srebrenica, where its exact deployments are and what their objectives and intentions are. As regards the 280th Brigade of the 28th Division in Srebrenica, was engaged in defence along the Bratunac-Potocari-Srebrenica axis. Its task was to defend, to persist in the defence of this axis, and later on to undertake measures as part of offensive activities towards Bratunac, and then to cut the Bratunac-Kravica-Konjevic Polje road from where it was supposed to pursue its military activities pursuant to the orders of the commander of the 28th Division. As regards the 281st Brigade, that brigade was closing the area, or rather, the axis Pod Gaj [phoen] Borovac, and its assignments, its task, within the overall offensive plan was to continue with its activities in the direction of Derventa and, further on, Milici. As regards the 282nd Brigade, it was engaged in the defence operations along the Zeleni Jadar-Srebrenica axis. As regards the offensive operations, it's task was to become engaged along the Zeleni Jadar and Skelani axis. The 283rd Brigade from the 28th Division, it was closing up the area Podravanje and Buce [phoen], along this axis here. Its task was to engage in offensive activities in the direction of Bracani, and further on to cooperate with the Zepa Brigade which was supposed to become involved here along this particular axis, and to pursue offensive operations in the direction of Derventa and Milici. 284th Brigade was covering the Ravni Buljim-Milicic route -- this is the axis I'm talking about -- and its task was to participate in the offensive activities and to attack along Ravni Buljim-Konjevic Polje axis, to cooperate with the 280th Brigade in order to cut up the Bratunac-Konjevic Polje communication and after that to continue with its activities in the direction of Cerska. The reserve forces of the 28th Infantry Division in the strength of one Mountain Battalion were deployed in the town of Srebrenica itself. They were ready to be used pursuant to the decision of the Division Commander, and the most likely axis of the use of these forces would have been as a step-up of the activities of the 280th and 284th Brigade, that is, after they cut up the Bratunac-Konjevic Polje route. The idea was to introduce these forces along that particular axis in the direction of Cerska. In accordance with the objective of the operation and in accordance with the tasks which were assigned by the Command of the 28th Division, the forces had to be joined with the forces that were attacking along the Tuzla-Zvornik axis.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, it was not my intention to have a detailed description of the deployment of forces, but let us say something about the tasks that the Drina Corps units were given, the units which were detached from their original units. Could you tell us something about their specific tasks? You don't have to go into details.

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have already referred to the decision of the Commander of the Drina Corps or, rather, the idea emanating from that decision, and that was to separate the two enclaves, Srebrenica and Zepa. The forces of the Drina Corps that were engaged for this operation had the task of gaining control of the feature Preda and to reach the line of Predala [phoen], Guber Banja, and then Zivkovo Brdo, Alibegovac, Kak -- Alibegovac, Kak. Once they reached this line, the forces of the Drina Corps would have carried out the task assigned to them by the Corps Commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So in effect, that would mean the completion of and the execution of the decision of the Commander.

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly. Thereby, the units of the Drina Corps would have carried out the task assigned to them by the Drina Corps Commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In this order, we see that some reserve forces have been planned, amounting to two to three companies of MUP and the 1st Company of the Vlasenica Brigade. Could you explain to us the tasks of a reserve force and what is implied by the concept of a reserve force in general in this order?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct that this order by the Corps Commander with respect to the reserves says that these reserves of the Drina Corps should amount in strength to two to three companies of MUP and one company of the Vlasenica Infantry Brigade. In all such documents for combat operations, the officer making such a decision also designates the reserve which may be introduced. He envisages such a reserve force, and depending on the situation, he would deploy it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, in this order, in the introductory part of that order, the commander is addressing to the 1st Zvornik Infantry Brigade, the 1st Bircani, the 2nd Romanija, the 1st Bratunac, the 1st Milici, and the 5th MUP, a MUP is being provided -- oh, I'm sorry, and the 1st MUP, so the MUP forces and the company of the Vlasenica Brigade. This order and the way it is written, is it being sent to these units as well which have been planned to form the reserve and to go into action as reserve force?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this order, as can be seen, the forces planned as reserves are not given this order for active combat action; therefore, not a single unit of the Ministry of the Interior received such a document, nor did the 1st Vlasenica Infantry Brigade, but only those units that are listed in the document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The 1st Vlasenica Brigade, or rather, one company from that brigade which had been planned as a reserve force, was it engaged in combat?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because of the extremely complex situation along the defence front for the Light Vlasenica Infantry Brigade where there was a constant threat of the front lines being broken through from the direction of Kladanj, I have already said that this brigade did not receive a copy of this order. However, because of the fact that the need arose on the 11th of July, the Corps Commander nevertheless decided to call on the commander of the Vlasenica Brigade to form a small unit of 50 to 60 men in addition to all the defence measures that need to be taken towards Kladanj, for that company to be brought to the region of Korc [phoen], which is east of the Srebrenica safe area, to take up positions of the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did the Corps Commander decide to use a part of this company after all which it had designated as a reserve?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were certain problems with the Bratunac Brigade because these were mostly elderly people, and they simply never made any progress throughout the time of the operation, and that is why the Corps Commander made such a decision and deployed this unit of 50 to 60 men in this particular area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, when the Corps Commander engages this unit from the reserve force, in this case, a company from the Vlasenica Brigade, did it then receive specific orders and specific assignments?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly so. The commander of that company is given a concrete task on the spot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We have another unit in reserve, and that is two to three companies of MUP forces. My first question is, were MUP forces informed at all about the preparations for the operation? Did they engage in reconnaissance together with you, and was a copy of this order sent to them?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assert with full responsibility that no one from the command structure in the area of the centre of -- covered by the centre of Security Services in Zvornik knew, even, that we were planning and preparing for this operation. They did not engage in any kind of reconnaissance, not when the Corps command engaged in reconnaissance, nor when brigades engaged in reconnaissance, and this was on the 4th of July. The rule as prescribed by our regulations is that when it comes to the engagement of MUP forces, the chain of command has to be strictly respected regarding a decision on the use of a particular unit, be it a MUP unit or a military unit.
